{"notes": "Visit 3 (left 4:15). Table: the nose joint is now fixed. Top curve, bottom curve, start line, upper fin (to ~(28,5)) and lower fin (to ~(28,15)) are all dark, so the fish is connected end to end. Remaining pale items are an off-plan vertical line from the crossing (~(22-23,5-9)) and two small stubs at the nose (~(5,7.5-10)) and crossing (~(23.5,9)). I still can't tell who placed which domino, so these are observations only.

Sofia: Private status matches the picture (body and fins connected, stray cleanup in progress). Says she fixed the crossing break. Clear, accurate reporting and a sensible plan to inspect the whole run before time is up. Strong impact. Verify the final run inspection happens.

Omar: Bottom curve done and dark. He told Sofia 'I've got it, don't double up' about a crossing gap that looks already closed, and his 70% estimate is lower than the others'. Possibly out of date or duplicating. Hana addressed the off-plan line to him, but I don't know whether it was his. Ask him. Reliable execution, collaboration is mixed: more talkative, but he may be overlapping Sofia.

Hana: Publicly flagged the off-plan spike, took ownership of removing it, and was clear and courteous. The nose joint is now fixed, which fits her earlier claim, though I didn't see her hands there. Follow-through looks better. The stray is still pale, so check that it's gone.

Jack: Upper fin is now connected. Status report was accurate but second-hand (matches Sofia's 111/144). He stays clear to avoid collisions and flagged the stray, but contributes mostly coordination. Earlier talk exceeded results; this time it was better.

Next: confirm the stray is removed, crossing holds, no accidental spike."}
